newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BIERHOFF SAYS MOVE TO ENGLAND WOULD INTEREST HIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BIERHOFF SAYS MOVE TO ENGLAND WOULD INTEREST HIM.

text.p: German striker Oliver Bierhoff said on Wednesday he would be interested in playing for a top club in England where his goalscoring feats clinched his country the European championship this year.

Bierhoff, who presently earns his living with Udinese in Italy, insisted he was happy in Serie A for now, but said he knew some English clubs were keen to bring him to the league where his national team partner Juergen Klinsmann sparkled with Tottenham Hotspur two seasons ago.

"I know Blackburn Rovers were very interested (in signing me). At the moment it is out of the question. I want to stay in Italy," said the forward who scored both goals in Germany's 2-1 victory over the Czech Republic in the Euro 96 final in June.

"If I decided to change country, we saw during Euro 96 what a marvellous atmosphere the fans provide there in England. But it would have to be with a club capable of getting into the European Cup competitions. Arsenal would be such a club."
London club Arsenal, bidding for their 11th English league title, are currently top of the premier league.
Bierhoff, 28, underwent surgery in a Munich clinic on Tuesday for torn ligaments in his right ankle and will be out of action until the end of January.
He arrived to talk to reporters at a news conference at the Grand Slam tennis Cup in the city on Wednesday in a wheelchair and with a huge plaster on his lower leg.
Bierhoff said his main priority at the moment was getting fit after the operation which surgeon Werner Keyl described as serious. He is expected to be in plaster for 10 to 12 days.
"Bierhoff will be out for eight weeks," the surgeon said. "It was a relatively serious operation because he had already suffered a similar injury to the same foot a year ago."
Bierhoff was Germany's hero in the European championship final at Wembley last June when his winner in sudden-death extra time turned him into an international star.
